entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Quintus Minucius Rufus was a Roman senator and military commander who played a pivotal role in the Second Punic War (218-201 BCE) against Carthage. As consul, he led successful campaigns against the enemy forces, capturing key territories such as Sardinia and Corsica.

Rufus's military victories were instrumental in securing Rome's dominance over the Mediterranean region, cementing its position as a major world power. His strategic leadership and tactical prowess earned him recognition among his peers, solidifying his legacy as one of Rome's most accomplished generals.

Despite his impressive achievements, Rufus's life was cut short when he died in 260 BCE at the age of unknown years, leaving behind a lasting impact on Roman history and the trajectory of Western civilization.
